title: KV shard playbook: notes + quick wins
content:
Purpose
- Brain dump after reading a few papers + internal benchmarks. Rough operational playbook for sharding KV state across devices/pods to reduce memory pressure and keep tail-latency reasonable.

Key intuition (TL;DR)
- For long-context apps the KV cache dominates memory. Instead of one big monolithic cache, treat KV like a distributed index: shard across machines by prefix-hash and fall back to local truncation for hot prefixes.
- Sharding reduces per-GPU memory but costs network hops for misses. Need hybrid policies: local hot-resident cache + remote shard for cold keys.

Notes from recent reads (quick links + takeaways)
- "FlashAttention" / kernel-level improvements: big wins on compute for attention but doesn't change KV memory footprint. Still important to reduce CPU-side overhead for streaming.
- "GShard" & routing papers: MOE-style routing for experts -> analogous idea: route KV lookups to the machine holding the shard (deterministic) to avoid scatter-gather where possible.
- Papers on sparse attention and locality: can often prune KV history for many tasks (dialogue) without retraining; good opportunity for aggressive TTLs per prefix.

Operational design primitives
1) Prefix hashing (deterministic shard map)
   - Use consistent hashing over token-prefix fingerprint (e.g., last-64-token rolling hash) to assign ownership.
   - Fast path: if request hits local prefix -> no network.
   - Slow path: request forwarded to owner shard (async/await streaming).
2) Hotset replication
   - Track per-prefix frequency (approximate count-min). Replicate top-K hot prefixes to every node to avoid network for high-QPS prefixes. Evict when cold.
3) Local stitching and truncation
   - For prefixes not found remotely quickly, fall back to local truncated KV (N most recent positions) to preserve low tail latency.
4) Lazy remote fetch + background prefetch
   - If slow path triggered, return partial continuation using local KV and start background fetch to warm local KV for subsequent requests.
5) Quantized storage for cold shards
   - Use 4-bit/8-bit compressed keys for cold shards saved to SSD/HBM-quantized to reduce memory. Serve via on-demand decompression.

Cost/latency tradeoffs matrix (notes)
- All-local (replicate everything): best latency, worst memory/cost.
- Sharded, no replication: best memory, worst tail latency on misses.
- Hybrid (hot replication + sharding): sweet spot if hotset is small (<5% of prefixes).

Prototype TODOs (priority sorted)
- [ ] Implement consistent-prefix-hash in toy harness (benchmark for 128k prefix space). Target: measure percent-local-hits for convo workloads. (owner: me)
- [ ] Add approximate frequency counter (CMS) and simulate hotset sizes across dataset (owner: Devon).
- [ ] Microbenchmark remote fetch latency (gRPC + direct RDMA if available), measure added token latency on miss. (owner: Maya)
- [ ] Evaluate compression artifacts: 8-bit vs 4-bit quant for KV vectors; check downstream generation quality with small prompt-holdouts.
- [ ] Add fallback policy in runtime: local-stitch -> partial-output -> background-warm. Gate behind feature flag.

Open questions / unknowns
- How to measure semantic quality degradation from quantized/partial KV? Need eval prompts that stress long-term co-reference.
- Network topology: would a two-tier network (rack-local preferred) be enough to keep tail-latency acceptable? Cost modeling needed.
- Consistency model for rollouts: when changing shard map, how to guarantee no double-serving or lost state? Must coordinate with rollout logic (canary + gradual rehash).

Quick heuristics for experiments
- Start with replication factor r = 3 for top-0.5% most popular prefixes, r = 1 otherwise. See how memory and latency behave.
- Use TTL per prefix = 10m for chat workloads, 1m for short burst workloads; adapt with EWMA of access interval.
- If remote-miss-latency > 15ms, serve partial from local truncation and emit telemetry event.

Metrics to record (instrumentation plan)
- prefix_local_hit_rate (per-model, per-region)
- avg_remote_fetch_latency (p50/p95/p99)
- generation_quality_delta_on_kv_compression (eval bench)
- memory_saving_vs_baseline (per-GPU)
- feature_flag_rollout_failure_rate (rebalance-induced errors)

Notes-to-self (writing-style half-scratchpad)
- Keep small experiments simple: synthetic workload with Zipfian prefix distribution to emulate hot prefixes.
- Correlate hot prefixes with customers/routes — avoid replicating prefixes that expose PII across nodes. Privacy check.
- Talk to infra about RDMA availability in dedicated clusters (might change remote fetch latency assumptions).

Useful links / papers to re-open later
- FlashAttention repo + perf notes (link pasted in PR)
- "Scaling Laws" (reminder: long-context costs scale nonlinearly with memory, not compute)
- MOE routing inspiration threads (internal notes in confluence link above)
- Internal GH: redwood/serving-runtime#4821 (KV cache eviction experiments)

Next meeting agenda (for sync with Maya/Devon)
- 10m: high-level design + safety/privacy concerns
- 20m: prototype plan + who owns microbenchmarks
- 10m: rollout strategy + feature flags
- 5m: immediate blockers (RDMA, KMS for prefix metadata)

End of dump — save and iterate.

-- aisha
